slot.brief: Solve a linear first-order ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) using the integrating factor method.

stem: For $x>0$, find the general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2}{x}y=\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$.

verdicts.working: The integrating factor is x², so (x²y)' = x sin x. Integrating gives x²y = sin x − x cos x + C, matching (A).

working:
$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int 2/x\,dx}=x^2$. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2y)=x\sin x$. $x^2y=\int x\sin x\,dx=\sin x-x\cos x+C$.

Independent check: The integrating factor is x², so (x²y)' = x sin x. Integrating gives x²y = sin x − x cos x + C, matching (A).
solution:
The integrating factor is $e^{\int 2/x\,dx}=x^2$ for $x>0$. Thus,
$$\frac{d}{dx}(x^2y)=x\sin x \quad\Rightarrow\quad x^2y=\sin x-x\cos x+C.$$
Hence $y=\dfrac{\sin x-x\cos x+C}{x^2}$.
